- [USER] User inquired about high-profile cases heard by the Supreme Court of India in recent years.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Sabarimala Temple Case: The Supreme Court of India allowed entry of women of all age groups into the Sabarimala Temple in Kerala, overturning a centuries-old tradition.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Aadhaar Card Case: The Supreme Court of India declared the mandatory linking of Aadhaar card with various services as unconstitutional and violative of the right to privacy.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Triple Talaq Case: The Supreme Court of India banned the practice of triple talaq, a Muslim divorce practice that allows men to divorce their wives by saying "talaq" (divorce) three times in a row.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Rafale Deal Case: The Supreme Court of India dismissed petitions challenging the Rafale fighter jet deal between India and France.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Section 377 Case: The Supreme Court of India decriminalized homosexuality by striking down Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code, which criminalized consensual gay sex.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Ayodhya Case: The Supreme Court of India ruled that the disputed site in Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh, will be given to Hindus for the construction of a Ram temple and an alternative land will be provided to Muslims for the construction of a mosque.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Reservation in Promotions Case: The Supreme Court of India upheld the constitutional validity of the policy of reservation in promotions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in government jobs.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The CBI vs. CBI Case: The Supreme Court of India ordered the reinstatement of CBI Director Alok Verma, who was removed from his post by the government.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Nirbhaya Case: The Supreme Court of India upheld the death sentence of four convicts in the 2012 gang-rape and murder case of a young woman in Delhi.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Electoral Bonds Case: The Supreme Court of India allowed the use of electoral bonds, which are anonymous donations made to political parties, but directed the political parties to disclose the identity of the donors to the Election Commission.
